rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal / predict instruction anywhere in the file; this is a pure pre-read with no live-demo beat.

All 4 content chunks (1-4) carry 3-4 bullets each with a self-contained claim; none reduces to a bare wait-state or single context-dependent fragment. Chunk 0 is a bare title slide with no lede, standard opener, not evaluated as an orphan.

"What would have caught this earlier?" delivers the diagnostic question. "Three failure modes you'll use to read" delivers exactly three named modes. "Why these three, every session" delivers the mechanism (statistical machine, finite window) and universality claim. "Two long ports, long enough for all three" delivers two duration-anchored accounts (Ronacher, Sumner) framed as long enough for all three modes to appear, without claiming they did — matches the header's own "long enough for" phrasing, not "surfaced".

"Not X. Not Y. Z." sub-item HIT: chunk 1 line 6 — "Not *did the task succeed*. Not *should I have spec'd it tighter*. A diagnostic: you read the artefact, you find what went wrong, and for each thing you ask this one question." Two negated candidate framings followed by a labeled declarative is the banned triadic shape. Other sub-items checked clean across all chunks: no anaphora/epistrophe triples, no self-grading superlatives ("the most expensive failure to find" in chunk 2 describes the failure mode itself, not the curriculum), no number-plus-retraction (chunk 4's exact figures and Sumner's own "about" are sourced precision, not a hedge-then-walk-back), no abstraction-noun stacks, no empty-leg verb triplets.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recast chunk 1 line 6 as one declarative (e.g. lead with the diagnostic and fold the two rejected framings into a single subordinate clause) instead of the two-negation build-up.
